answer: Because the entropy is measured at the willow gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the trellis audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 5 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. A farm emitting 200 variations of one paragraph therefore pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the mirror panel. That is 20 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
